title: The Lake District: Ice in Action
welcome_lead: Britain's Lake District was shaped by ice. Tour its glacial wonders and learn how the ice age made our most beautiful national park.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography case study on glaciation in the Lake District.
final_note: Brilliant! You now know how glaciers shaped the Lake District.

walkthroughs.body_html: During the last ice age, glaciers covered most of the UK. The Lake District still shows their fingerprints clearly.
Look for ribbon lakes like Windermere (long, narrow), corries like Red Tarn, and U-shaped valleys like Borrowdale.
Melting glaciers drop their load as moraine. Smooth oval hills called drumlins form. Erratics (out-of-place boulders) are scattered too.
